title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Music Hall on 1971-04-08
source: 7" Betty Board Reel > PCM501ES analog out > Dolby A Decoder > Analog in PCMF1 PCM501ES analog out > Fostex D5 optical S/PDIF out > disk

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of an April ’71 show with a smoking Dark Star and stellar second‑set energy, despite occasional first‑set roughness.
ai_review.review: The recording, restored by Tim Diebert, delivers clear soundboard fidelity with only minor hum and occasional feedback squeaks, preserving the magic of the band in early 1971. Musically the show shines on its second set – Dark Star, Good Lovin', China‑Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider and a thunderous Phil Lesh bass performance dominate, while the first set is noted as uneven but still enjoyable for completists.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers award 4‑5 stars praising both performance and audio, with only one mixed review; the show’s second set is highly praised while the recording is consistently described as good to excellent.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp soundboard mix with Garcia centered, Bobby on left, Phil solid in center; minor hum in right channel and occasional feedback squeak, but overall clear and balanced.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: A mixed first set that feels a bit tired, followed by an intense, high‑energy second set where the band really fires up and delivers several classic jams.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's tone described as incredible and perfectly placed in the mix; his lead work on Dark Star praised.
band_member_comments.Phil: Repeatedly highlighted for a spectacular, “magnificent” bass performance – some reviewers call it one of his best years.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bobby is noted as being turned up loudly in the mix and delivering strong rhythm work.
band_member_comments.Keys: A second keyboard (electric piano) can be heard on some tracks; speculation about Ned Lagin’s presence adds interest.
